headline: 15,717 children reported missing across Bangladesh Jan-July 2026; 2,038 still untraced
summary: Police Headquarters revealed that 2,038 children, accounting for 13% of the total, remain untraced after being reported missing between January and July this year.
details: A total of 15,717 children were reported missing across Bangladesh between January and July this year, according to Police Headquarters (PHQ). Of these, 13,679 children were rescued or returned to their families, but 2,038 remain untraced.

The untraced children account for 13 percent of the total missing reports. PHQ disclosed these figures to clarify previous media reports that did not mention the subsequent status of the missing children, which could lead to public confusion.

Police verification through respective stations shows that 474 children aged between zero and nine years were reported missing from January to July. Of them, 406 were rescued, while 68 are still untraced.
For the 10 to 17 years age group, 15,243 children were reported missing during the same period. Among them, 13,273 were rescued, with 1,970 remaining untraced.

PHQ also noted a significant increase in general diaries (GDs) related to missing persons since the introduction of online GD services. Data shows 17,808 missing-person GDs in 2023, 16,414 in 2024, and 22,550 in 2025.

For the 10 to 17 years age group, 15,243 children were reported missing during the same period. Among them, 13,273 were rescued, with 1,970 remaining untraced.

headline_marked: [[73 Bangladeshis face ACC scrutiny]] over alleged Dubai money laundering
headline: 73 Bangladeshis face ACC scrutiny over alleged Dubai money laundering
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission is seeking information from the UAE government regarding properties allegedly acquired through illicit financial transfers, including by a former minister and bank chairmen.
details: Bangladesh's Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) is set to request information from the UAE government concerning properties in Dubai. This inquiry involves 73 Bangladeshis, including former land minister Saifuzzaman Chowdhury and former bank chairmen HBM Iqbal and Chowdhury Nafis Sarafat, over alleged money laundering.

The ACC plans to send a Mutual Legal Assistance Request (MLAR) to the UAE under the United Nations Convention against Corruption (UNCAC). This mechanism facilitates cooperation between member states by exchanging information and documents in corruption and financial crime investigations.

According to ACC sources, the individuals under investigation are suspected of acquiring flats and houses in high-end Dubai areas such as Dubai Marina and Palm Jumeirah. Many of them also reportedly obtained the UAE’s Golden Visa.

ACC Deputy Director Aktarul Islam stated that the investigation team recently wrote to the Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) for information on these assets. The team has also gathered data from various other government agencies, including the Election Commission and National Board of Revenue.

This extensive investigation follows a Supreme Court directive issued on January 16, 2023. The directive mandated the ACC and other relevant authorities to probe allegations concerning assets acquired in Dubai by 459 Bangladeshi citizens.

Data from the Centre for Advanced Defense Studies (C4ADS) and the EU Tax Observatory indicated that as of 2020, 459 Bangladeshis owned 972 properties in Dubai. These properties were recorded with an estimated value of around $313 million, highlighting the scale of alleged illicit financial flows.
